tools.name: create_pond
tools.description: Mint a new Pondchat room (pond) for video/audio/chat. Returns room URL and WebSocket endpoint. This is the only way to create a room — for metadata of an existing roomId, use get_room_info (read-only). Note: a custom roomId is not reserved — if another pond already uses it, you share the same door.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Post a text message into a Pondchat room. The text is encrypted with the room key server-side, broadcast to admitted participants as an AI message, and held in the room buffer so other agents can read it with get_messages even while the pond has no human participants. Use this to write; use get_mess

tools.name: get_messages
tools.description: Read recent room chat: persisted chat history plus the AI-message buffer, merged by time and decrypted server-side (the roomId is the read capability — same trust model as send_message). Use for WHAT was said; use list_participants for WHO is present. Works on rooms that are not host-moderated or lo

tools.name: get_room_info
tools.description: Static metadata for an existing roomId: URL, WebSocket endpoint, capacity. Read-only — does NOT create or activate the room (use create_pond to mint), and does not verify the room is live: for liveness use list_participants or GET /api/room/{roomId}/state.

tools.name: list_participants
tools.description: List who is currently in a live Pondchat room: admitted humans (userId + display name) and AI participants (aiUserId + display name), plus recentAgents — MCP agents that posted to the room buffer recently (works on empty ponds, ~1h window). Use for WHO is present; use get_messages for WHAT was said.

tools.name: close_pond
tools.description: End a live room session: disconnects all participants and wipes the room contents (chat history, AI messages). Use when a pond must be force-emptied — do NOT call it to "delete" a room: the roomId stays a stable re-joinable door either way, and an abandoned pond cleans itself (buffers expire in ~1h,

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "send_message" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: create_pond, send_message, get_messages, get_room_info · Public sink: create_pond, send_message · Destructive: close_pond.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: create_pond, send_message, get_messages, get_room_info · Public sink: create_pond, send_message · Destructive: close_pond

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
